title: Compound Poisson Distribution
author: John Robin Inston
date: 2026-09-25

title-block-banner: true
---

Let $S_{N}=X_{1}+\dots _+X_{N}$ be the sum of i.i.d. terms where the number of
terms $N$ is random and follows a Poisson distribution
$N\sim \mathcal{P}(\lambda)$. The random variable $S_{N}$ follows a **compound
Poisson distribution** with PGF given by
$$
G_{S_{N}}(t)=e^{\lambda(G_{X}(t)-1)}.
$$
`\begin{proof}`
The proof of this result follows from past results in our summary of
[[probability-generating-functions|probability generating functions]].`\end{proof}`

For the sum of i.i.d. Bernoulli RVs $X_{i}\sim \mathcal{B}(1, p)$ the PGF is
given by
$$
G_{S_{N}}(t)=e^{\lambda((p(t-1)+1)-1)}=e^{\lambda p(t-1)},
$$
hence $S_{N}\sim \mathcal{P}(\lambda p)$.
